statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-14672 (PostgreSQL observable response discrepancy with non-default scram_iterations provides user existence oracle) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 16.15: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14672/ lists 16.15 as the fixed release for major version 16, and the 16.15 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.15/, include it. Alpine's postgresql16 16.15-r0 is the upgrade to upstream 16.15 and lists CVE-2026-14672 under its secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from that APKBUILD and the upstream source release of the same version, and the postgres server binary in every published build (16.13-r0, 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, reports the matching PostgreSQL 16 release. PostgreSQL says versions before 16 are unaffected; this owner publishes PostgreSQL 16, and the scram_iterations setting the flaw depends on is present in the server binary of every published build for Alpine 3.23. The earlier published builds for Alpine 3.23 (16.13-r0 and 16.14-r0) are built from earlier upstream releases, their server binaries report those older versions, and Alpine's secfixes do not list this CVE for them, so they are recorded as affected; 16.15-r0 and later carry the fix.

CVE-2026-14672 (PostgreSQL observable response discrepancy with non-default scram_iterations provides user existence oracle): an unauthenticated user can test whether a role exists when that role has a non-default SCRAM iteration count, because the mock authentication challenge for a nonexistent role always used the default iteration count. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14672/ lists 17.11 as the fixed release for major version 17, and the 17.11 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.11/, list this CVE. The fix on the REL_17_STABLE branch is https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/dec60e8ada4cd46d0201efea844a4b22cb06444e (Security: CVE-2026-14672, in tag REL_17_11 and not in REL_17_10), which changes mock_scram_secret() in src/backend/libpq/auth-scram.c to use the scram_iterations setting instead of the built-in default, and adds a note to the scram_iterations documentation. Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD on the 3.23-stable branch, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/ce22298320177ae25085d86fbf3b4fc1150c16a2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD, lists CVE-2026-14672 under 17.11-r0 in its secfixes. The DHI postgresql17 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD on that branch and the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; the current 17.12-r0 build uses the APKBUILD at that commit, and none of its patches changes the file the fix changes, nor do the patches of the 17.11-r0 APKBUILD on that branch. We read every published postgresql17 package for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0) on x86_64 and aarch64, checking each against the repository index checksum: /usr/libexec/postgresql17/postgres in each reports the PostgreSQL release matching its package version. 17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0 and 17.10-r0 are built from PostgreSQL releases before 17.11 and are affected; 17.11-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix. The fix makes the mock challenge use the server's scram_iterations setting; as the updated PostgreSQL documentation says, a role whose password was created with an iteration count different from the server's scram_iterations setting can still be discerned, so passwords should be created with the configured value.

CVE-2026-14672 (PostgreSQL observable response discrepancy with non-default scram_iterations provides user existence oracle): an unauthenticated user can test whether a role exists when that role's password uses a non-default SCRAM iteration count, because the mock authentication challenge for a nonexistent role always reported the default iteration count. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14672/ lists 18.6 as the fixed release for major version 18, and the 18.6 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.6/, list this CVE. The fix on the REL_18_STABLE branch is https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/822143c4d1dce62a43b98341eacbd4429eca7e59 (Security: CVE-2026-14672, in tag REL_18_6 and not in REL_18_4), which changes mock_scram_secret() in src/backend/libpq/auth-scram.c to use the scram_iterations setting instead of the built-in default, and documents the remaining behaviour. PostgreSQL 18.5 was never released (the 18.6 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.6/, say so), so although Alpine's security database lists this CVE for postgresql18 under 18.5-r0, this owner has no 18.5-r0 build and its first build that carries the fix is 18.6-r0. The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built with Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD from the 3.23-stable branch of aports (current revision https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD) and the upstream PostgreSQL source release of the same version; none of the patches that APKBUILD applies, at any revision used for these builds, changes the files this fix changes. As of 2026-11-28 the DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository publishes builds of source postgresql18 at 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0, for x86_64 and aarch64. We read every one of them on both architectures, with package checksums verified against the repository index, and in each the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql18/postgres, reports the PostgreSQL release matching its package version. The fix changes one assignment and adds no message or symbol that marks it in the binary, so the per-build evidence is the release each server binary reports. 18.6-r0 is the first published build for Alpine 3.23 that carries the fix, and 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0 carry it. The earlier published builds (18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0 and 18.4-r0) are built from PostgreSQL releases before the fix and are affected. As the updated PostgreSQL documentation for scram_iterations says, a role whose password was created with an iteration count different from the server's current scram_iterations setting can still be discerned, so passwords should be created with the configured value.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-14672, an observable response discrepancy in SCRAM authentication that lets an unauthenticated user test whether a role with a non-default scram_iterations exists, in 17.11. Within major version 17, releases before 17.11 are affected. Versions before PostgreSQL 16 are not affected. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14672/, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.11/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.11-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6438-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-14672. The fixed version is this owner's first rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1, which packages PostgreSQL 17.11 and is no longer in the repository. Every build published now carries the fix: the postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 17.11 in the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 and in the 17.11-1 build, and PostgreSQL 17.12 in the 17.12-0 build and in the rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1, on amd64 and arm64. The earlier rebuild of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, packages PostgreSQL 17.10; it is affected and sorts below the fixed version.
